# wallix.bastion.config_smtp

Manage the SMTP configuration of a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Update the global SMTP server settings the Bastion uses to send its emails (notifications, alerts).
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_config_smtp` Terraform resource.
- The SMTP configuration is a singleton that always exists on the Bastion and has no delete endpoint, so the module only offers [`state=present`](#parameter-state). Removing the Terraform resource does not change the Bastion either.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-authentication-method"></a>**authentication_method** | `str` | Authentication method, for example `off`, `on`, `plain`, `login`, `SCRAM-SHA-1`, `CRAM-MD5`, `DIGEST-MD5` or `ntlm`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-certificate-hash"></a>**certificate_hash** | `str` | Hash of the SMTP server certificate. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-password"></a>**password** | `str` | Password to authenticate to the SMTP server with.<br>The Bastion does not return it, so it cannot be compared. See [`update_password`](#parameter-update-password). |
| <a id="parameter-port"></a>**port** | `int` | TCP port of the SMTP server. |
| <a id="parameter-postmaster-email"></a>**postmaster_email** | `str` | Email address of the postmaster. |
| <a id="parameter-protocol"></a>**protocol** | `str` | Protocol used to reach the SMTP server, for example `smtp`, `smtps` or `starttls`. |
| <a id="parameter-sender-email"></a>**sender_email** | `str` | Email address the Bastion emails are sent from. |
| <a id="parameter-sender-name"></a>**sender_name** | `str` | Display name of the sender of the Bastion emails. |
| <a id="parameter-server"></a>**server** | `str` | Host name or IP address of the SMTP server. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Only `present` is supported. The SMTP configuration cannot be deleted.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default) |
| <a id="parameter-update-password"></a>**update_password** | `str` | `on_create` sends [`password`](#parameter-password) only when the Bastion reports that no SMTP password is set yet (the configuration itself always exists, so this is the equivalent of "on creation").<br>`always` sends [`password`](#parameter-password) on every run, which then always reports a change.<br><br>Choices: `always`, `on_create` (default) |
| <a id="parameter-user"></a>**user** | `str` | User to authenticate to the SMTP server with. |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion. The module sends the current values of the unset options with the changed ones, because the API refuses an update that lacks one of [`protocol`](#parameter-protocol), [`authentication_method`](#parameter-authentication-method), [`server`](#parameter-server), [`postmaster_email`](#parameter-postmaster-email), [`sender_name`](#parameter-sender-name) and [`sender_email`](#parameter-sender-email).
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Send the Bastion emails through the corporate relay
  wallix.bastion.config_smtp:
    protocol: starttls
    authentication_method: plain
    server: smtp.example.com
    port: 587
    postmaster_email: postmaster@example.com
    sender_name: WALLIX Bastion
    sender_email: bastion@example.com
    user: smtp-user
    password: "{{ vault_smtp_password }}"

- name: Change only the sender name
  wallix.bastion.config_smtp:
    sender_name: Bastion PROD
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated. Contains `password` when it was sent.<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: `["sender_name"]` |
| <a id="return-config-smtp"></a>**config_smtp** | `dict` | The SMTP configuration as returned by the Bastion API after the change, without the password.<br>In check mode, the expected configuration.<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-config-smtp) |

<a id="sample-config-smtp"></a>

### Sample of `config_smtp`

```yaml
authentication_method: plain
certificate_hash: ''
port: 587
postmaster_email: postmaster@example.com
protocol: starttls
sender_email: bastion@example.com
sender_name: WALLIX Bastion
server: smtp.example.com
user: smtp-user
```
